system.summary: Cardinal d'Este's cipher (Tomokiyo): letters as symbols and figures with homophones (a = rho, epsilon, barred f, large looped rho; e = small s, 18, dumbbell...), nulls (M, Z) and code signs ([Roy], [le pape], [qui], [Monsieur], [faire], [pour]).
system.notes: Shape names and three values fixed on glossed pages of Colbert 338 (pp. 435-438, 453-454, 504).

prior_solution.where: The key: S. Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, 'Cardinal d'Este's Cipher (1584-1586)' (henryiii.htm), built on BnF fr. 16041-16042; Colbert 338 not cited, no letter edited. The text of p. 523: no edition found; Favalli, CHMO 49/2 (2024), read, covers 1569-1580 and does not mention it; Favalli's thesis (HAL tel-03435435, 1559-1580) not read in full. Catalogue 1572 open on origin/main (GitHub API, e2315f8a, 5 Nov 2026). p. 517 (13 Nov 2026): no edition found; one web search on Poigny / Montmorency / Joyeuse / Clermont-de-Lodève 1584 found nothing printing this advice. pp. 513 and 518 (13 Nov 2026): p. 513's cipher block is deciphered in the margin by a contemporary hand (our reading agrees); no edition of either page found (three web searches: Luigi d'Este's letters to Henri III / Villeroy, Longlée, Desjardins' Négociations avec la Toscane - its tome IV prints the Florentine envoys' dispatches, not d'Este's French letters; not checked page by page).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target, set the rules (protocols and amendments hashed before each computation, one measurement on a held-out page, thresholds fixed in advance) and answered the blind shape sheet (shapes only). AI agents transcribed, applied and adjusted the key, measured, read and wrote up. No palaeographer checked the page.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Tomokiyo's d'Este table applied to Colbert 338; shape names fixed on glossed pages 435-438, 453-454, 504.
Five tests against the volume's contemporary glosses (V1-V5): best V2 p. 504, 0.777 characters vs 0.332 (thresholds 0.85/0.75); V4 and V5 not admissible (glosses not literal).
Probable words from a list fixed in advance placed on the training pages only: alpha with a descending tail = f; key K-C01 frozen.
One measurement on held-out p. 523: M5 0.457 vs 0.078 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (gap 0.379); thresholds >= 0.60 and >= +0.30.
Read by sense after a blind shape sheet of 14 questions: 200 words, 146 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 22 unresolved (88.5%).
Cryptiana re-read; Favalli 2024 read in full; Favalli's thesis (HAL tel-03435435) not readable; web searches for an edition of fr. 16041-16042 or of this advice: nothing.
Probable words placed on pages already seen only (pp. 436-438, 453-454, 504, 523): sig = m, A = [fait], Venus sign = [faire], newt = nn; key K-C02 frozen and hashed.
One pre-registered measurement on held-out p. 517 lines 4-29 (979 signs): M5 0.509 vs 0.067 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (gap 0.442); thresholds >= 0.45 and >= +0.30 fixed before.
p. 517 read by sense: 231 words, 201 certain, 22 probable, 3 restored, 5 unresolved (96.5%).

Integration check (PR #546): own decoder from key-p517.tsv equals decryption-p517.txt on all 29 lines; M5 re-implemented from validation.txt gives 0.509 against best control 0.068 (median 0.025) on lines 4-29; about 110 signs of lines 1, 2 and 20 agree with the Gallica image (IIIF f272). Frozen files not in the PR (key-p517.tsv is a later copy: 98ef85f6 vs frozen aa7d73db), order of events by the contributor's record. Strict recount by the README bar: p. 517 201/231 = 87.0%, p. 523 146/200 = 73.0% (probable, restored and unresolved words are holes); contributor's 96.5% and 88.5% kept as theirs. Both pages read in part.

Values for new and contradicted shapes taken from p. 517 (after its measurement) and p. 518 (training page): Venus sign = o, barred dumbbell = null, y = [Espagne], four new shapes; key K-C03 frozen and hashed with a pre-registration naming p. 513 as held-out block.
Pre-registered test on p. 513 not run: the frozen block has 208 signs, under the 300 required by the pre-registration; K-C03 stays unvalidated and its values are given as probable.

p. 518 read by sense with K-C02 and the probable values: 108 words, 87 certain, 16 probable, 1 restored, 4 unresolved (95.4%, after a blind shape sheet of 14 Nov 2026; 94.4% before); the letter pp. 517-518 together 326/339 = 96.2%.
p. 513 cipher block read: 47 words, 38 certain, 5 probable, 4 unresolved (91.5%); checked against the contemporary margin decipherment, which agrees and gives 'Espaigne' for the code word y.

outcome.method_basis: Read with Satoshi Tomokiyo's published d'Este table, adjusted on glossed and already-read pages of the same volume (keys K-C01, K-C02); K-C02 passed a pre-registered held-out test on p. 517 (bar 0.45, lowered from 0.60 before the test, by the contributor's record); the code word y and two signs (Venus sign, barred dumbbell) stay open. pp. 518 and 513 (after PR #546) read with K-C02 unchanged plus probable values for new shapes (key-p518-513.tsv); the pre-registered test of these values (K-C03) could not run (p. 513 too short).
outcome.fraction_read_source: README read bar applied strictly at integration (13 Nov 2026), per page, never pooled: p. 523 146/200 = 73.0%, p. 517 201/231 = 87.0% (certain words only; probable, restored and unresolved words are holes). fraction_read is p. 523, the page first written up. The contributor's figures (Daniel's rule as they applied it, certain + probable): p. 523 177/200 = 88.5%, p. 517 223/231 = 96.5%. pp. 518 and 513, added after PR #546, counted by the same strict rule: p. 518 87/108 = 80.6%, p. 513 38/47 = 80.9%; contributor's figures: p. 518 103/108 = 95.4% (letter 326/339 = 96.2%; 101/107 = 94.4% before the blind shape sheet of 14 Nov 2026), p. 513 43/47 = 91.5%.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out tests (not docs/_validate.py). p. 523 (5 Nov, key K-C01): M5 0.457 vs 0.078, partial (thresholds 0.60 / +0.30). p. 517 lines 4-29 (13 Nov, key K-C02, thresholds 0.45 / +0.30 fixed before from the clear texts of the volume): M5 0.509 vs 0.067, validated. Integration check (13 Nov 2026): no M5 script in the PR; an own re-implementation from the description gives M5 0.509, best control 0.068, median 0.025 on p. 517 lines 4-29 (code words spelled out). The p. 517 bar (0.45) was lowered from p. 523's 0.60 before the test, by the contributor's record; the frozen pre-registration, key file and block are not in the repository (the committed key-p517.tsv is a later copy: it hashes to 98ef85f6, the frozen value is aa7d73db).

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 517, whole page in cipher
texts.summary: The writer hears that the pope was told, from the court of T(urin?), that 'this duke' had letters from the King of [Spain] urging him to make war on the King and protect Marshal de Montmorency; he doubts it, explains Montmorency's fears of Joyeuse around Clermont-de-Lodève and his letters to [Spain], and hopes Poigny's mission has calmed him, as the levy of 4,000 foot in the State of Milan has melted away.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 13 Nov 2026 by one AI reader: 201 certain, 22 probable, 3 restored, 5 unresolved of 231 words (96.5%), each probable word justified in reading-p517.md; the code word y restored as Spain by sense only. No palaeographer checked the page.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share at integration (13 Nov 2026): 201 certain of 231 words = 87.0%; the 22 probable, 3 restored (Espagne twice, the code word y by sense; que) and 5 unresolved words are holes. The contributor's figure, certain + probable, is 223/231 = 96.5% ('read').

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 518, lines 1-16 in cipher (end of the letter of p. 517)
texts.summary: End of the p. 517 letter: the writer asks that the news be referred to His Majesty and doubts it bodes well for the pacification with Montmorency; going to his audience before closing his letters, he discussed Languedoc with the Pope, who ordered him to do all he can so that the King comes to terms with Marshal de Montmorency to calm the troubles.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 13 Nov 2026 by one AI reader, updated 14 Nov 2026 after a blind shape sheet answered by Brice Dudout (L1 '6' = plain o): 87 certain, 16 probable, 1 restored, 4 unresolved of 108 words (95.4%); each probable word justified in reading-p518.md; new shapes take probable, unvalidated values. With p. 517 the letter is 96.2%. No palaeographer checked the page.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share (README read bar, as at the integration check of PR #546): 87 certain of 108 words = 80.6%; the 16 probable, 1 restored and 4 unresolved words are holes. The contributor's figure, certain + probable, is 103/108 = 95.4% (after the blind shape sheet of 14 Nov 2026; 101/107 = 94.4% before); with p. 517 the letter is 326/339 = 96.2% by that count.

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 513, cipher block of the letter of 2 January 1585
texts.summary: Luigi d'Este reports that, according to the sieur de Longlée, in Spain they are scheming in case the Church changes its shepherd (the pope dies), strengthening their designs and weakening those of others, and that express orders have been sent to Rome; a matter of great importance for the King's service. Already deciphered in the margin at the time.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 13 Nov 2026 by one AI reader: 38 certain, 5 probable, 4 unresolved of 47 words (91.5%); the contemporary margin decipherment, looked at after the transcription was frozen, agrees word for word where legible.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share (README read bar, as at the integration check of PR #546): 38 certain of 47 words = 80.9%; the 5 probable and 4 unresolved words are holes. The contributor's figure, certain + probable, is 43/47 = 91.5%.

texts.label: Colbert 338 p. 523, whole page in cipher
texts.summary: A prince (name in a code word, not read) had the pope asked for the title of king and was refused; he turned to the emperor; the writer was told the emperor alone gave Cosimo of Florence his grand-ducal title; he asks that the King be told and that his source among the pope's people stay secret.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5 Nov 2026 by one AI reader; Brice Dudout answered the shape sheet only. The decryption construes as French sentences with gaps: 146 certain, 31 probable, 1 restored, 22 unresolved of 200 words (88.5%), so read in part.

texts.note: read_share is the strict share at integration (13 Nov 2026): 146 certain of 200 words = 73.0%; 31 probable, 1 restored and 22 unresolved words are holes. The contributor's figure, certain + probable, is 177/200 = 88.5%.
